recent_posts.title: Securing CI/CD for an open source project: lessons from Cilium
recent_posts.summary: Cilium's security team details how they harden their CI/CD pipeline against supply chain attacks. Key controls include: SHA-pinned GitHub Actions and container images, a custom bot (Ariane) restricting who can trigger builds, two-phase checkouts for pull_request_target workflows to isolate untrusted code, Go module vendoring so dependency changes appear as reviewable diffs, CODEOWNERS gates on all .github/ changes, Renovate with a 5-day cooldown for automated dependency updates, static analysis via actionlint and CodeQL to catch expression injection and missing permissions, CI vs. production credential isolation using protected environments, and keyless Sigstore Cosign signing with SBOM attestations. The post also honestly documents remaining gaps: no SLSA provenance, no govulncheck in CI, 68 internal @main references, and no dependency-review-action. It closes with a look at GitHub's 2026 Actions security roadmap and how planned features like dependency locking, scoped secrets, and native egress firewalls map to current workarounds.

recent_posts.title: Understanding Kubernetes Networking
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to Kubernetes networking fundamentals, covering the IP-per-Pod model, flat network structure, CNI plugins, and how packets move between pods on the same and different nodes. The guide explains Kubernetes service types (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, ExternalName, Headless), service discovery via cluster DNS, and virtual IPs. A significant portion focuses on Cilium as a CNI, detailing how it uses eBPF to replace iptables/kube-proxy for higher performance, identity-based security, transparent encryption, and observability via Hubble. Native routing vs. overlay/encapsulation modes are compared with trade-offs discussed.

recent_posts.title: Celebrating 10 Years of Cilium: What’s New and What’s Next
recent_posts.summary: Cilium marks its 10th anniversary with over 60% CNI market share, 1,010+ contributors, and 24,000 GitHub stars. Key highlights include the Cilium 1.19 release featuring ztunnel mTLS integration, expanded IPv6 support, stable Multi-Pool IPAM, smarter DNS policies, and Hubble flow log aggregation. New production case studies from OVHcloud and Zynga showcase real-world impact — Zynga eliminated conntrack scaling issues by replacing kube-proxy with eBPF-based load balancing. A new O'Reilly book 'Cilium: Up and Running' and a children's illustrated guide are now available. The project is positioned as the networking data plane for AI workloads, with Microsoft and Google using it for large-scale AI training clusters.

recent_posts.title: Cilium at Cloud Native Days France 2026
recent_posts.summary: A first-person recap of Cloud Native Days France 2026, a 1,700-attendee event in Paris. Highlights include a CERN keynote on scaling to 10 PB/s of data with flat budgets, French government open-source Kubernetes initiatives, and multiple Cilium-focused sessions covering ClusterMesh multi-cluster networking, Direct Server Return with eBPF, and a hands-on lab platform that has served 100,000+ sessions. The post also covers community interactions, hallway conversations about Cilium and Tetragon in production, and notable talks on k0s, VictoriaLogs, supply chain security, and sustainable cloud native infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: Cilium Networking & eBPF-Powered Security Policies on RKE2
recent_posts.summary: A detailed guide on replacing RKE2's default Canal CNI (Calico + Flannel) with Cilium to gain eBPF-powered networking and security. Covers why iptables-based CNIs hit performance walls at scale, how Cilium's eBPF datapath achieves O(1) policy lookups via kernel hash maps, and step-by-step instructions for both fresh installs and live Canal-to-Cilium migrations using Helm. Also covers CiliumNetworkPolicy for L3/L4/L7 enforcement, Hubble for real-time observability, common troubleshooting scenarios on RKE2, and a feature comparison table between Cilium, Canal, and standalone Calico.

recent_posts.title: Day 2 with Cilium: Small configurations that keep large clusters boring
recent_posts.summary: Datadog shares operational practices for running Cilium across hundreds of Kubernetes clusters at enterprise scale. Key recommendations include using native routing over overlays, tuning IPAM parameters with surge allocation to prevent pod scheduling delays, implementing strict upgrade gates with preflight validation and connectivity tests, monitoring BPF map pressure as an early warning signal, and configuring kube-proxy replacement with Maglev hashing. The post emphasizes treating cloud APIs as critical dependencies, maintaining stable identity cardinality through label allowlists, and using kernel-level tools like bpftrace for debugging datapath issues that don't surface in standard metrics.

recent_posts.title: 2026 Kubernetes and Cilium Networking Predictions : @VMblog
recent_posts.summary: Kubernetes networking is evolving rapidly in 2026, driven by organizations migrating away from VMware and adopting AI workloads. Key trends include running VMs on Kubernetes through KubeVirt (though with a steep learning curve), the emergence of "Kubernetworkers" who blend traditional networking with cloud-native skills, and networking adaptations for GPU-heavy AI workloads requiring topology awareness and high throughput. Microsegmentation is becoming urgent again, with eBPF and Cilium enabling identity-aware enforcement. The convergence of traditional and cloud-native networking is reshaping how teams approach connectivity, security, and observability in Kubernetes environments.

recent_posts.title: Tetragon: An End-of-Year 2025 Reflection
recent_posts.summary: Tetragon, an eBPF-powered runtime security tool, achieved significant milestones in 2025 including Windows support preview, persistent enforcement during agent failures, flexible enforcement modes for testing policies, attribute resolution for easier policy writing, and userspace hooks (uprobes/USDTs) for application-level visibility. The community grew through conference talks, user stories from production deployments, and technical blog posts demonstrating real-world adoption in Kubernetes clusters and cloud-native environments.

recent_posts.title: SuperSkyRay, Part 1: Running Ray AI Apps Across K8s Clusters for Resource and Time Efficiency
recent_posts.summary: SuperSkyRay enables Ray AI applications to run across multiple Kubernetes clusters using KubeRay and Cilium Cluster Mesh for multi-cluster networking. The Nova K8s fleet manager handles cross-cluster placement, allowing workloads to leverage resources from different clusters simultaneously for improved resource utilization and execution efficiency.

recent_posts.title: Linux Kernel Fundamentals for Effectively Writing Tetragon Tracing Policies
recent_posts.summary: Explores essential Linux kernel concepts needed to write effective Tetragon tracing policies. Covers kernel vs user space, system calls, hook points (kprobes, tracepoints, LSM hooks), process management, file descriptors, and networking sockets. Provides practical examples of how kernel fundamentals translate into monitoring policies for security observability, with guidance on choosing appropriate attachment points for different scenarios.
